summaries.summary: OpenAI's developer platform, organized as an organization containing projects and kept separate from ChatGPT workspaces, whose roles do not carry over. Preset roles are Org owner, Org reader, Project owner, Project member and Project viewer, with effective access the union of held roles; changes take up to 30 minutes to propagate. Agents should run as project service accounts, ideally via workload identity federation, with model allowlists, spend limits and permissions like api.model.request. API data is not used for training by default.

OpenAI's asynchronous batch endpoint, costing 50% less than synchronous calls with a separate, higher rate-limit pool and a 24-hour completion window only. It covers Responses, Chat Completions, embeddings, completions, moderations and image endpoints, with up to 50,000 requests and a 200 MB input file per batch and 2,000 batches per hour. Outputs expire after 30 days by default, and per-model queued-token caps appear only in Platform settings.

OpenAI's older chat endpoint, /v1/chat/completions, still supported as of 2026-11-14, though Responses is recommended for new projects. Requests are stored by default for new accounts, and store=true cannot be set in non-US data-residency regions. It remains a supported Batch endpoint and also works with the remote MCP tool.

OpenAI's hosted evaluation product, which became read-only for existing users on 2026-10-31 and shuts down on 2026-11-30. Teams building agents should not adopt it: the deprecations page names Promptfoo as the replacement, while the Evals guide points to Datasets.

OpenAI's frontier models (GPT-5.x) and Codex, which OpenAI and Oracle announced on 2026-06-10 would be offered through OCI Marketplace, payable with eligible Oracle Universal Credits (secondary source). Go-live and the model list were not confirmed, and it is unconfirmed whether they are live in OCI Generative AI itself or only via OCI Marketplace.

OpenAI's GPT models as hosted on third-party data platforms, notably Databricks Foundation Model APIs and Snowflake Cortex. Databricks hosts GPT-6.1 Terra and Sol, GPT-6 Sol, Luna and Astra, GPT-5.x and GPT OSS, though some are hidden from AI Playground. In Snowflake Cortex, GPT-6 models went GA on 2026-11-06; openai-gpt-6.1-sol is GA except private preview in AI Functions, 6.1-terra is preview, gpt-4.1 is legacy, and availability of 5.6 and later varies by account.

OpenAI's flagship API model family: gpt-6-astra, gpt-6.1-sol, gpt-6.1-terra and gpt-6-luna. Astra is the most capable and recommended default; 6.1-sol is near-Astra at lower cost; 6.1-terra is fast and suited to visual reasoning, computer use and writing (cutoff Jun 1 2026); Luna is the most efficient for high volume. Knowledge cutoffs range from Apr 30 to Jun 1 2026.

OpenAI's open-weight chat models, offered on OCI Generative AI as openai.gpt-oss-120b and openai.gpt-oss-20b since 2025-11-18. On-demand access is limited to the Chicago, Frankfurt and Osaka regions. gpt-oss-120b is the default NL2SQL model in OCI Generative AI Agents, and Oracle EPM's in-product LLMs use GPT-OSS through OCI Generative AI.

OpenAI API mutual TLS: once a trusted certificate is activated for an organization or project, every API request in that scope must present an accepted client certificate in addition to its bearer credential. Configuration is governed by the api.mtls.read and api.mtls.write permissions, with write needed to change it. mTLS cannot be combined with OpenAI Private Link.

OpenAI's private connectivity option that reaches regional OpenAI API endpoints from Azure VNets via southcentralus, westus, eastus2 and spaincentral privatelink hosts. It is not self-service and must be granted through OpenAI sales. It is incompatible with IP allowlist controls and mutual TLS, so agent deployments must choose one network control approach.

The OpenAI API Platform identity for agents and deployed apps, jobs and CI, belonging to a single project and created via the Admin API at /organization/projects/{project_id}/service_accounts. Only Org owners and Project owners can manage them. The create_service_account_only option yields an account with no roles or key that cannot call models until granted permissions. Least-privilege setups pair it with a custom role, model allowlist, spend limit and workload identity federation via a service account mapping.

OpenAI's low-latency speech and realtime API, GA since 2025-08-28; the beta interface (OpenAI-Beta: realtime=v1) was removed on 2026-05-12. Browsers connect via WebRTC at /v1/realtime/calls using ephemeral secrets from /v1/realtime/client_secrets, while servers use WebSocket. It supports functions, MCP servers and connectors, and outbound SIP calling for GPT-Live opened to all organizations on 2026-11-02.

OpenAI's recommended API for new projects and agent work, replacing the shut-down Assistants API together with the Conversations API; the Python Agents SDK uses it by default. Responses are stored for 30 days unless store is false, which ZDR organizations enforce. Built-in tools include web search, file search, tool search, remote MCP, function calling, shell, skills, computer use and image generation. State carries via Conversations or previous_response_id, but instructions must be resent each turn and chained input tokens are rebilled.

The Responses API mcp tool type, which lets OpenAI models call remote MCP servers over Streamable HTTP or HTTP/SSE, with Secure MCP Tunnel for private servers and remote server_url replacing connector_id. Approval is required by default via mcp_approval_request/response items. OAuth tokens in authorization are not stored and must be resent on every request. Limits are 1000 RPM on Build and 2000 RPM on Launch/Grow, with only token costs; it is ZDR-compatible and also works in Chat Completions.

OpenAI's HTTP API at api.openai.com/v1, authenticated with a Bearer API key or a workload-identity access token, with OpenAI-Organization and OpenAI-Project headers selecting scope; admin endpoints need an Admin API key. Clients should honor Retry-After and x-ratelimit headers, ramp traffic gradually above 1M input TPM, and keep headers under 64 KiB and file inputs under 50 MB. Revoked keys stop within seconds, but other auth changes take up to 15 minutes.

OpenAI's official Terraform provider, openai/openai, authenticated with OPENAI_ADMIN_KEY, for managing API Platform configuration as code. Resources such as openai_project_model_permissions and openai_project_hosted_tool_permissions set per-project model allow/deny lists and control file search, web search, image generation, remote MCP and Code Interpreter. It also exposes project data-retention modes, including zero_data_retention and modified_abuse_monitoring variants.

OpenAI API Platform usage tiers, now Free, Build, Launch and Grow, replacing Tier 1-5; organizations start on Free self-serve and upgrade automatically as credit purchases grow. Monthly usage limits are $100 (Free), $500 (Build, $5 purchased), $5,000 (Launch, $100) and $200,000 (Grow, $500). Rate limits scale by tier, for example Build at 5,000 RPM and 1M TPM for Astra/Sol/Terra, up to Grow at 15,000 RPM and 40M TPM.

OpenAI's keyless auth for the API: a workload exchanges a short-lived OIDC JWT, SPIFFE JWT-SVID or X.509 certificate for a short-lived access token mapped to a project service account via a service account mapping. It is configured under Organization Settings > Security > Workload Identity Provider, with documented providers including Kubernetes, AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, OCI, GitHub Actions and SPIFFE. Tokens have no refresh token, so repeat the exchange. Codex support is in beta via federation rules.

OpenAI's Zero Data Retention mode, which excludes customer content from abuse logs and forces store to false; it requires prior OpenAI sales approval and can be set per organization or project. Eligible endpoints include Chat Completions, Responses, embeddings, audio, moderations and realtime. Conversations, assistants, threads, vector stores, files, fine-tuning, evals and batches are not eligible, which constrains agent designs needing stored state. Private Safety Processing is a variant.

The OpenAPI specification for describing REST APIs, used across agent platforms to define tools. Microsoft 365 declarative agents call OpenAPI-described APIs as actions, Foundry supports OpenAPI tools in network-isolated setups, and Power Platform custom connectors accept only OpenAPI 2.0, not 3.0. Snowflake REST APIs are OpenAPI-compliant, and Oracle's EPM Agent Skills ship 22 OpenAPI-style YAML definitions.

Snowflake's Apache NiFi-based data integration service, with connectors for SharePoint, Google Drive, Box, major databases, Kafka, Kinesis, Salesforce, Slack, Jira, Workday and more, useful for feeding agent data. The Snowflake Deployment runs on SPCS and is GA in AWS, Azure and GCP commercial regions, with BYOC GA on AWS. New deployments are gen 2 (connector configuration in public preview), and it is not auto-enabled on trial accounts; the account team must enable it.

OpenID Connect, the OAuth-based identity standard behind SSO and keyless workload federation across platforms. Microsoft Entra and OpenAI workload identity federation both trust short-lived OIDC tokens from external issuers. OCI identity domains support OIDC for compliant apps, Snowflake supports OIDC sign-in with Google, Entra ID and custom providers such as Okta, and Salesforce supports OIDC SSO through Auth. Providers (unverified).

OpenTelemetry, the open observability standard used by agent platforms for tracing. Google's Agent Runtime has enabled OpenTelemetry tracing by default for newly deployed ADK agents since 2026-06-18. AWS AgentCore Observability is OTEL-compatible, Databricks MLflow traces build on it, and Salesforce Agentforce session tracing can be exported via OpenTelemetry in beta.

Oracle's long-term support database release, announced 2025-10-14 as the successor to Oracle Database 23ai via the October 2025 release update, requiring no upgrade or recertification. AI Vector Search is included at no extra charge, and OCI Generative AI Agents can use bring-your-own 26ai vector search as a RAG knowledge base. On-premises Linux x86-64 GA arrived with the January 2026 RU 23.26.1.

Oracle's managed autonomous database service, renamed from Autonomous Database in October 2025, with version 26ai replacing 23ai. It offers Select AI for natural-language-to-SQL (runsql, showsql, explainsql, narrate, chat) and, on Dedicated Exadata since 2026-02-03, Select AI Agent for agents, tools, tasks and teams. Each database can expose a managed remote MCP server for 26ai and 19c, and a PL/SQL OCI SDK is preinstalled on Serverless.

Oracle's managed database service, now renamed Oracle Autonomous AI Database (October 2025), with 26ai replacing 23ai. Agents can authenticate with IAM database tokens after enabling OCI_IAM external authentication and granting a policy on autonomous-database-family; instance and resource principals map through dynamic groups. Network access options are public with optional ACL, allowed IPs and VCNs only, or private endpoint only.

Oracle's public cloud, where a tenancy is the root compartment holding all resources and users, groups, dynamic groups and federation are managed at tenancy level. OCI has no dedicated agent identity type, so agents use existing principals. OCI Generative AI is its enterprise AI platform with hosted models, OpenAI-compatible endpoints, a Responses API and hosted agents, alongside the older Generative AI Agents service. Official SDKs cover major languages, and new Cloud EPM and EDM subscriptions run on OCI IAM.

Oracle database services running in AWS, bought through an AWS Marketplace private offer negotiated with Oracle sales (or a public offer, such as Autonomous Database Serverless) and linked to a new or existing OCI tenancy. Onboarding creates a MulticloudLink_AWS base compartment and policies that must not be changed or deleted. Access is managed through predefined OCI groups such as aws-db-family-administrators and aws-network-administrators.

Oracle database services running in Azure, bought by accepting a private offer in Azure Marketplace and then linking or creating an OCI tenancy, with billing through Azure Marketplace. Access maps Entra ID groups to Azure roles and replicated OCI groups, for example odbaa-exa-infra-administrators to the Exadata Infrastructure Administrator role. Setup requires an Entra ID Administrator and an OCI Identity Domain Administrator.

Oracle's Enterprise Data Management (EDM) cloud service; new subscriptions run on OCI using OCI IAM. Oracle Fusion AI Agent Studio can reach EDM REST APIs using the same Trusted confidential application pattern as Cloud EPM. EDM uses only the Service Administrator and User roles, so Power User or Viewer grant nothing, and all operations are blocked during the daily maintenance window.

Oracle's Planning business process in Cloud EPM, with a long line of built-in AI features. These include Predictive Planning (16.12), Auto Predict (20.08), IPM Insights with GenAI summaries and Bring Your Own ML (21.11), Predictive Cash Forecasting (24.04) and Advanced Predictions (25.08). The newest is Reporting Agent, GenAI Q&A over report grids, released in 26.07.

Oracle's agent-building environment for Fusion applications, which hosts, monitors and evaluates EPM Assistants, agent teams that call Cloud EPM REST APIs scoped to each user's EPM roles. Connecting to Cloud EPM or EDM requires an Identity Domain Administrator to create a Trusted confidential application with client credentials and JWT assertion and an imported certificate, set up under Credentials > Data Source Applications with SSO in place. It can also use OIC MCP servers, though without identity propagation.

Oracle's cloud Enterprise Performance Management suite (formerly EPM Cloud), sold via Oracle Sales in Standard and Enterprise tiers and running on OCI IAM. Automation runs as an identity domain user, usually Service Administrator, via Basic Auth or user-context OAuth, with no workload identity federation or agent identity type. Private connectivity uses an OCI Service Gateway, not VPN. Agents integrate through REST, EPM Automate, EPM Agent Skills or AI Agent Studio EPM Assistants; there is no official MCP server or SDK, and monthly updates hit test before production.

Oracle Integration (OIC), Oracle's integration platform, which since OIC 26.01 lets projects register integrations as agentic AI tools and build agents from a project AI tab. Each project exposes an MCP server at a per-instance mcp-server/v1/projects URL supporting tools/list and tools/call in all OIC regions. Supported LLM providers, consuming external MCP servers and A2A support are unconfirmed.

The per-project MCP server exposed by Oracle Integration, supporting tools/list and tools/call in all OIC regions. Auth is OAuth 2.0 with OCI IAM, and callers need a confidential app with the ServiceInvoker role. An integration appears as a tool only if it is Active in a project, triggered by an OAuth REST Adapter with a JSON payload, and registered as an agentic AI tool. Fusion AI Agent Studio can consume it, preferably over Streamable HTTP.

Oracle's official GitHub repository (github.com/oracle/mcp) of about 33 local MCP servers for OCI, including oci-cloud, compute, networking, identity, database, MySQL and GoldenGate, but none for EPM. Its README states it is not intended for production use, and some servers may not work with token-based auth alone. The recommended general-purpose server is oracle.oci-cloud-mcp-server.

The recommended general-purpose OCI MCP server in Oracle's oracle/mcp repository, run with uvx oracle.oci-cloud-mcp-server@latest. Its SDK-backed tools let agents discover and invoke any OCI API (find_oci_api, describe_oci_operation, invoke_oci_api and others). In stdio mode it authenticates through OCI config and OCI_MCP_AUTH_TYPE options such as api_key, instance_principal or resource_principal; in HTTP mode it uses an IDCS confidential app with scope oci_mcp.cloud.invoke.

Snowflake's legacy organization administrator role, being phased out for multi-account organizations in favor of GLOBALORGADMIN in the organization account. It can be enabled in up to eight accounts by default. Snowflake promises at least three months' email notice before removal, with no date published as of 2026-11-14. ORGADMIN cannot set CORTEX_ENABLED_CROSS_REGION.

Microsoft Power Platform's code-first web apps (React, Vue and others) hosted on Power Platform that call 1,500+ connectors from JavaScript. An admin must enable them per environment, and end users need Power Apps Premium, pay-as-you-go, an App Pass or auto-claim. They lack Power Platform Git integration, SAS IP binding and SharePoint forms support, and are managed with the pa CLI.

Microsoft Power Automate's cloud workflows, where each trigger and action consumes one Power Platform request and every flow is capped at 100,000 requests per five minutes. Limits currently apply per flow, but a phased switch to per-user limits starting April 2027 may throttle flows. Runs last up to 30 days, synchronous requests time out at 120 seconds, and idle flows can be turned off after 90 days. Flows can be irreversibly converted to agent flows with Copilot Credits.

Microsoft's low-code platform, organized as tenant > environment group > environment > optional Dataverse database, with roles differing by whether Dataverse exists. Automation options include GitHub Actions for Power Platform for solution import/export and environment provisioning, and the microsoft/power-platform Terraform provider (latest v4.2.1, 2026-10-19). IP Firewall and customer-managed key prerequisites are unconfirmed.

Microsoft's Entra admin role for Power Platform, which manages all environments, bypasses environment security groups and manages data policies and tenant isolation, but cannot create users or assign licenses. Its authority is scoped to Power Platform, unlike tenant-wide AI or Global Administrator, and it grants no Dataverse data access without self-elevation or PIM. It must allow-list non-Microsoft clients for the Dataverse MCP server, and registered Power Platform API service principals act with its power.

An Entra app registered with Power Platform for automated admin access, created and registered with pac admin create-service-principal, which also adds it as an application user (System Administrator by default) and prints the secret once. It cannot register itself; an admin with user context must register it. Once registered it acts with Power Platform Administrator-level power, and granular roles cannot be applied, so it is not least-privilege.

Microsoft's pac command-line tool for Power Platform, current version 2.15.1, installable via VS Code, MSI or the .NET tool, though the .NET tool lacks pac data and package deploy. pac auth create supports interactive, device code, service principal, managed identity and GitHub or Azure DevOps OIDC federation. pac copilot manages Copilot Studio agents as local files, and pac copilot mcp runs a built-in local MCP server. It also underpins Build Tools for Azure DevOps 2.0.

Power Platform connectors that wrap custom APIs for apps, flows and agents, defined from OpenAPI 2.0 only or a Postman collection, with a definition file under 1 MB. Auth can be OAuth 2.0, API key or Basic, but not client credentials, and OAuth connectors use a per-connector redirect URI since February 2024. Each connection allows 10,000 requests per minute, and users can create up to 50 on a per-user plan.

Power Platform's connector guardrails, formerly titled data loss prevention policies, governing Power Apps, Power Automate and Copilot Studio connectors at tenant or environment scope. Because agent MCP access goes through connectors, these policies govern MCP too. Enforcement can take up to 24 hours, and violating apps, flows and agents are suspended with connections disabled.

The Power Platform container for apps, flows and agents, holding zero or one Dataverse database. Without Dataverse it has only two roles: Environment Admin, which adds users, provisions Dataverse and creates data policies, and Environment Maker, which creates apps, connections, custom APIs and flows without data access.

A Power Platform control, set by a Power Platform Administrator, that blocks inbound and outbound cross-tenant connections for Entra-authenticated connectors in canvas apps and flows. It is configured in the admin center under Security > Identity and access, with up to 500 allowlist rules by tenant ID or domain, taking about an hour to apply. The Azure DevOps connector is not enforced by it.

A Google Cloud Gemini consumption option (preview) that charges a per-token premium over Standard PayGo for more consistent throughput with no commitment; responses report ON_DEMAND_PRIORITY as the traffic type. Its ramp limits were removed on 2026-09-10. Supported endpoints (global only, or global plus us/eu) differ between documentation versions.

Google's managed RAG pipeline in Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, renamed from Vertex AI RAG Engine on 2026-04-22, covering ingestion, chunking, embedding, indexing, retrieval and grounded generation from local files, Cloud Storage and Google Drive. It is backed by a managed, billed Spanner instance and supports CMEK and VPC-SC but not data residency or Access Transparency. Several US regions need an allowlist for new projects, and quotas include 60 RPM for data management and 600 RPM for retrieval.

The OpenAI-style Responses API as offered by other clouds. Amazon Bedrock serves it, with Chat Completions, on bedrock-runtime at /openai/v1, but rejects background=true and application inference profiles and has no server-side tools. In Microsoft Foundry, stored Responses data stays in the customer's geography with AES-256 and optional customer-managed keys, and external code can call it directly as an ephemeral agent.

The Google Cloud IAM role for Gemini Enterprise Admin, named as such since 2026-04-15 and mapped to the Discovery Engine role ID. It grants Discovery Engine Editor plus admin-only rights such as setting agent IAM policies, which agentspaceUser can only propose, and transferring shared-agent ownership. It is required to register ADK agents in Gemini Enterprise and is typically granted with Service Usage Consumer and Logs Viewer by a project owner.

Salesforce's CRM platform, where the org is the tenancy unit; editions are now Core, Advanced and Max, bought through an account executive. Agent work needs an external client app, a dedicated Integration user and provisioned Agentforce, Einstein and Data 360 licenses; there is no keyless workload identity federation, so CI uses the JWT bearer flow. Enterprise orgs get 100,000 daily API calls plus 1,000 per license, with long-running concurrent requests capped at 25 and REQUEST_LIMIT_EXCEEDED past the hard cap.

Salesforce's sf command-line tool (v2; sfdx v7 is frozen), latest stable 2.158.7, needing Node.js 22+ for npm installs and delivering Agentforce DX. It authorizes orgs via web login or JWT through an external client app, and sf org create agent-user creates Einstein Agent Users. sf agent commands publish authoring bundles, preview, run evaluation tests and register external MCP servers (developer preview). Since 2026-10-28 it always redacts secrets from output.

Salesforce's classic OAuth app registration, now superseded by external client apps: creating new connected apps has been restricted since Spring '26 and requires Salesforce Support, though existing ones keep working. Since September 2025 uninstalled connected apps are restricted to users with an approval permission, so agent apps must be installed and allowlisted before go-live. A connected app is still needed to run scratch or sandbox creation from an authorized Dev Hub.

Salesforce's free, non-commercial developer org, which has included Agentforce and Data Cloud (now Data 360) since March 2025 and, from April 2026, Agentforce Vibes IDE, Claude Sonnet 4.5 as default coding model and hosted MCP servers. It gets 15,000 API calls per day and can expire if nobody logs in, losing Dev Hub package versions. Data and LLM-call limits cited by one blog are unverified.

Salesforce's recommended OAuth app type (ECA), replacing connected apps and required for agent integrations alongside a dedicated Integration user. A PEM certificate enables the JWT bearer flow for CLI and CI. Agent API setup needs scopes api, refresh_token, chatbot_api and sfap_api with client credentials and JWT-based tokens enabled, while hosted MCP needs the mcp_api scope. Pre-authorization uses AdminApprovedPreAuthorized with profiles or permission sets.

Salesforce's consumption currency for Agentforce, introduced May 2025 and metered per agent action. They list at $500 per 100,000 credits, with a standard action costing 20 credits (about $0.10) and a Voice action 30. Credits are bought Pre-Purchase, PayGo or Pre-Commit through the account executive and tracked in Digital Wallet. The $5/user/month Agentforce User License requires Flex Credits.
